claim: the global shore is the ENVELOPE of the top-coefficient conditions: for every level n the first gamma at which any coefficient turns negative is >= gamma_shore(lam), with equality approached exactly at the argmin level k*
method: the beta-mean formula (verified 248/0 against the exact knife engine): the sign of knife m is the sign of one polynomial at X = s^2, so the threshold in gamma is found by exact bisection per coefficient

margin_profile.reading: a sharp minimum exactly at n = k*, growing away from it in both directions. At the minimum the BINDING coefficient is the top one (m = N-1), whose condition is exactly the published T_n.

what_this_reduces_the_theorem_to: at n = k*: binding is the top coefficient, condition exactly T_n -- already published
away from k*: the margin exceeds 1 and grows -- this is what needs proving
refuted_today_by_my_own_test: the stronger guess that the binding coefficient is ALWAYS the top one is FALSE: at (n=24, lam=1) coefficients 15, 16, 20, 21 turn negative below that level's own shore, and similarly at (30,3), (40,2), (15,1/5), (12,50). Interior coefficients CAN bind before the level's own top -- but never, on any cell measured, before the GLOBAL shore.
why_the_suggested_experiment_was_aimed_w: the incoming note proposed working down from the top at d = 2, 3, 4. Measured: the d=2 threshold sits 3 to 18 times ABOVE the shore, so that end carries no difficulty at all.
